### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx`  _(via DatasetMeasureSchema (symbol, a top-level const), won_amount (literal, a string literal in a comment in DatasetMeasureSchema))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e7fab738fba59c613828049f7ee4bd222ed049b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `acd7c86a9587aeddafd4b1bcfb3f067b2175513b` — the merge of head `9425caec3933f8a37ea843f7a8faca5665799eed` into base `7e7fab738fba59c613828049f7ee4bd222ed049b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin acd7c86a9587aeddafd4b1bcfb3f067b2175513b && git checkout acd7c86a9587aeddafd4b1bcfb3f067b2175513b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7e7fab738fba59c613828049f7ee4bd222ed049b 9425caec3933f8a37ea843f7a8faca5665799eed && git checkout -B drift-repro 7e7fab738fba59c613828049f7ee4bd222ed049b && git merge --no-ff 9425caec3933f8a37ea843f7a8faca5665799eed

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e7fab738fba59c613828049f7ee4bd222ed049b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7e7fab738fba59c613828049f7ee4bd222ed049b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: 108/108 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3ed391abf9f717f1be723d9064d8bb19ba9c1c74`

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Both carriers refuse on save exactly what the door refuses at chart, both directions.** Probed at head with tsx against the REAL door (`normalizeAnalyticsFilterTree({ where })` from `service-analytics` source; core stubbed for one temporal predicate only) and `DatasetSchema`: 27 targeted rows agree (implicit, `$eq`, empty list, two hops, under `$and` / `$or` / `$not` / `$not` over `$or`, null-prototype spec, class instance carrying `$eq`, dotted inner key). Carrier message equals the door's byte for byte after removing only ` at where.PATH`; door envelope `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. Controls agree: a `$`-keyed spec, `$and` or `$not` inside a field spec, `$nor`, Map comparand, `$ne` list, `$in`, scalar, null, empty relation, other arms — door accepts or refuses with a DIFFERENT sentence, carrier raises no equality issue. Seeded fuzz, 3000 filters: door equality-refused 2243, carrier 2243, 0 mismatches, 0 sentence differences. Top-level list reported once; `top + nested` yields exactly two distinct issues. The PR's 68 pins pass locally at head. Base tree: every nested shape parses `success: true`.
2. **Ruling A untouched.** `data/filter.zod.ts` absent from the diff; `FilterConditionSchema.safeParse` on both nested shapes still `success: true` at head. The walk mirrors `mapWhereFieldEntries` clause for clause (arrays under `$and` / `$or`, `$not`, other `$` keys skipped, `isNestedRelationSpec` prototype test). Published shape: `z.toJSONSchema` of `DatasetSchema` / `DatasetMeasureSchema` hash-identical head vs base (refinement sits on the `.optional()` wrapper, so nothing is cloned).
3. **Baseline.** `collectDroppedRefinements` at head: `ui/Dataset` = "", `filter`, `filter.lazy`, `include.element`, `measures.element.filter`; `ui/DatasetMeasure` = `filter`, `filter.lazy`; base lacks the three new sites. Dataset is embedded in exactly 4 published manifest schemas (baseline grep), each gaining 2 sites: 8+2+1 = 11; header 574 to 585, matched by `dropped-refinements.test.ts`, which reads only the two counted fields. `Lint & Repo Gates` (check:generated) green.
4. **DELIBERATE CORRECTION.** Both notes exist on `origin/main` unconsumed (blobs `d819b05` / `d27f042`; added by `14add487b4` and `6aa3188a39`; spec CHANGELOG top is 17.4.0, both notes newer).
   - `.changeset/19889-filter-schema-door-array-equality.md`. OLD: "is not judged, because the face does not judge it either. The analytics `where` door does refuse that shape when a dataset or measure filter is charted." FALSE on landing (the two carriers judge it on save). NEW: "is not judged by `FilterConditionSchema`, because the face does not judge it either. The analytics `where` door does refuse that shape, because it flattens the relation to a dotted member. So the two carriers that door charts, the dataset `filter` and the measure `filter`, refuse it on save as well, in the same words. That is a separate change in this release, ADR-0087 entry `dataset-filter-nested-relation-equality-array-refused-at-save`." TRUE at head; one bullet moved, rest byte-identical.
   - `.changeset/19888-analytics-implicit-array.md`. OLD: "One position is judged only here: a list inside a nested relation … A document carrying that still publishes, and it is refused when it is charted." FALSE ("only here", "still publishes"). NEW: "One position is judged here and not by the shared authoring schema … A dataset `filter` or measure `filter` carrying one is refused when it is saved, in the same words (a separate change in `@objectstack/spec`, ADR-0087 entry `dataset-filter-nested-relation-equality-array-refused-at-save`). Any other `where` that reaches this door with one, such as a caller `where` or a dataset selection's `runtimeFilter`, is refused only when it is charted." TRUE (`dataset-executor` line 1075 folds `selection.runtimeFilter` into the door's `where`; the request doors parse `FilterConditionSchema` only, which does not descend). One paragraph moved, rest identical.
   - `Check Changeset` annotations name exactly these two files with the two-class text; the red is the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class, no `skip-changeset` label.
5. **Major-18 entries.** `…-refused-at-save` reason, OLD "(1) … refuses it when a dataset or measure filter is charted." — false as stated now; NEW "refuses it when the filter is charted; a dataset filter and a measure filter refuse it on save as well, which is the sibling entry dataset-filter-…-at-save." — true. Acceptance criteria gain "A dataset filter or a measure filter is the exception: its nested-relation lists are refused on save too (…)." — true. `…-refused` reason, OLD "(that door alone also refuses a list inside a nested-relation condition …); and, on SAVE, the schema door (…), which is the sibling entry …-at-save." — false (save now also refuses via the carriers); NEW "(that door alone, among the runtime doors, …) … plus the two carriers that analytics door charts (a dataset filter and a measure filter) inside a nested relation too, which is dataset-filter-…-at-save." — true; `read-scope-sql` refuses any nested-relation value outright with its own sentence, so "alone among the runtime doors" holds.
6. **New changeset, ADR-0087 entry, docblocks.** Every checked claim true at head: base shapes green at `9e7824a445`; charting on every path (objectql-strategy 199/254/480/532, native-sql 451/486, preview via `normalizeWhereComparands`); issue paths `filter.account.region` and `measures.0.filter.account.region.$eq` confirmed; `$ne` unjudged; `$in: []` kept; accepted filter returned unchanged. Route right: accept-set narrowing of a published authoring schema, no D2 conversion, own entry because the surface is two carriers in one position. Registry region equals the entry file modulo indent, inserted in id order (`data-nosql…` sorts before it, `dataset-measure…` after). Major-18 entries are not in `spec-changes.json` / the upgrade guide (0 hits for the existing `…-at-save` id), so no projection moves.

### ② Semver level
Correct: `minor` + `**BREAKING**` + `!` + `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` + `adr-0087: registered …`. AGENTS.md rule 3: "(narrowing) is BREAKING"; `check-changeset-no-major` ships breaking as `minor` in the launch window; `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the narrowing arm as breaking signal (4) and finds the marker. `Clause-②: no` is right: no key, export or operator is widened. Both gates inside the green `Lint & Repo Gates`.

### ③ Boundary flags
- Other arms (`$gt: null`, `$in: 'won'`, `$between: [null, 5]`), top level and nested: carrier accepts, door refuses with the face's other-arm sentence — reproduced; #19889 / #20116 family, not this card.
- Caller `where` and selection `runtimeFilter` with a nested list: refused at chart only, loud to the requester; objectui widget / report routes NOT MEASURED here either.
- `refinementSitesThatDidProject` 369: no reader; the 409 figure not re-measured here (gen:schema not rerun).
- PR body `Clause-②: no` beside changeset `no (narrowing)`: level axis reads `not-declared`, exit 0; ADR gate reads the changeset; mirrors #20047 — consistent, two spellings of one line.
- `$nor` and a `$`-keyed field spec pass save and fail at chart with non-equality sentences — pre-existing, outside this card.
- CI at head: 32 checks success or skipped, Test Core 6/6 green, `Check Changeset` failure x2 (the deliberate class above).

Head-sha: `9425caec3933f8a37ea843f7a8faca5665799eed`

The analytics `where` door does refuse that shape when a dataset or measure filter is charted." FALSE on landing (item 2). That is a separate change in this release, ADR-0087 entry `dataset-filter-nested-relation-equality-array-refused-at-save`." TRUE (items 2, 5). Only that bullet moved.

FALSE ("only here", "still publishes"). NEW: "judged here and not by the shared authoring schema … A dataset `filter` or measure `filter` carrying one is refused when it is saved, in the same words (… `dataset-filter-…-at-save`).
